Hi Samir — quick technical follow-up on sizing and burst behavior (summary + recommended defaults).

Quoted for context:
> On Mon, 2 Mar 2026 at 09:05 Samir Gupta <samir@nebula-analytics.com> wrote:
> > - Pool sizing: why start at 4x A100-equivalent? Is that to meet peak throughput only?
> > - Burst clauses: we need clarity on how bursts are priced and the operational notice required.

Answers / recommendations:
- Baseline recommendation: 4x A100-equivalent to support sustained throughput of ~2.2M tokens/hour for your current models (based on the sample prompts you shared). That gives headroom for concurrency and KV cache reuse without swapping.
- Eval credits: the 2000 GPU-hours are total evaluation hours applied to the reserved pool or shared burst pool — effectively covers a 2–4 week aggressive eval depending on concurrency. We can instrument metering so you can see consumed eval-hours.
- Burst mechanics: default burst = up to 2x baseline for short windows (capped at 200 hours/month). Bursts are subject to available spare capacity in the region; with Dedicated we provide a best-effort guarantee and an SLA-backed fallback to compatible model variants if we cannot supply full burst levels.
- Operational notice: recommended standard notice = 24 hours for bursts up to 1.5x; 72 hours for sustained bursts >1.5x. We can shorten notice with a higher reserved commit or a premium burst SLA.
- Pricing impact: short bursts (<=200 hrs/month) priced at usage rate; sustained bursts (>200 hrs/month) billed at reserve rate for any incremental baseline increase.

I attached a simple capacity_pricing_sheet.csv that maps commit tiers to per-GPU-hour rates and shows example monthly invoices for 6 / 12 / 24 month terms.

If that looks good, Marissa can fold the numbers into a commercial term sheet.

Thanks,
